text:
nate: Heads-up — onboarding Kestrel-v1-ptq into the invocation pipeline. Canary ran 10k requests and we see ~0.9% of function invocations failing due to malformed JSON suffixes (trailing comma / stray ‘\u200b’). Repro snippet below. Anyone seen this pattern before?

lina: Ugh, saw similar with an earlier PTQ pass where tokenizer emitted stray zero-width spaces. Did you capture raw tokens?

nate: Yep, attached top failure example from logs: 
```
response: {
  "action": "create_ticket",
  "params": {
    "title": "Cluster OOM",
    "priority": "high",
  },
}
```

nate: Parser errors are coming from strict JSON path in the function router, which then triggers a retry. Our retry budget burns fast -> downstream rate limits.

rohit: Can we add a small postprocess sanitizer in the canary that runs a heuristic strip for trailing commas and invisible chars before parse? Keep it off by default.

amanda: +1 for a configurable sanitizer. Need to measure false positives — some tool responses intentionally include explanatory text after JSON. If we strip aggressively we might mask real schema drift.

lina: Two quick probes: (1) run strict-mode (fail on any non-json) vs (2) relaxed-sanitizer (strip trailing commas, remove \u200b, balance braces) and compare parse_success and semantic-equivalence.

eval-bot: Bench results (canary-2026-03-19): 10k samples each. Strict parse success: 99.12%. Relaxed sanitizer success: 99.95%. Semantic equivalence (automated diff of required fields): strict 99.05%, relaxed 99.02%. Latency delta: +4ms p50 for sanitizer.

rohit: Those numbers suggest sanitizer fixes most noisy PTQ outputs and doesn't hide much drift. But that 0.03% delta in semantics could be real. We need a triage queue for sanitizer-rescued responses.

nate: Agreed. Proposed rollout: enable sanitizer for canary traffic (5% of prod) with tagging of rescued responses to an audit log and daily sampling for manual review. Also bump retry budget slightly for canary to avoid cascading rate-limits while we evaluate.

amanda: Add an instrumentation flag so SDK emits `x-parse-repaired: true` header when sanitizer runs. That will make downstream telemetry easy.

sre-bot: Note: increasing retry budget may increase 429s if we don't backoff properly. Recommend exponential backoff with jitter and a per-route cap.

lina: On the model side, I want to rerun PTQ with a tokenizer-clean pass (strip zero-width, normalize unicode) and re-evaluate. If that reduces sanitizer hits we can prefer fixing model pipeline.

nate: Action items: 
- @lina run tokenizer-clean PTQ and post benchmark (due EOD)
- @rohit implement sanitizer toggle + audit tagging in router (PR)
- @amanda add header flag in SDK (tiny PR)
- @sre-bot will propose new retry/backoff defaults for canary routes

rohit: I'll open PR with sanitizer heuristics today. Will include configurable rules and a debug endpoint to show original vs repaired payload.

nate: Thanks — if sanitizer looks good I'll hold canary at 5% for 72h and then reassess parse failure, latency, and semantic drift.

amanda: If we find the 0.03% semantic delta tied to tokenization fixes, we should prefer model-fix over long-term sanitizer. But short-term sanitizer buys time. :thumbsup:
